pool.text: A Spanish garrison was posted near the foot of the Laventille Hills.
The Spanish garrison was captured during Walter Raleigh's expedition in April.
French naval commander Comte d'Estrées visited and reported no Port of Spain.
Spanish governor Don Sebastien de Roteta reported in writing to the King.
The alcalde of Trinidad reported native abuse of the Holy Faith.
The Cedula of Population encouraged settlement of French Catholics in the island.
Ann's River course was diverted to run east of the city.
An offshore fort was completed to serve as the defence.
The Deep Water Harbour Scheme dredged the offshore western neighbourhoods area.
A five-route trolleybus system started serving the city.
Local dance legend Beryl McBurnie established one of the oldest theatres.
Queen's Hall was built through efforts of the music community.
Marine Square was officially renamed to Independence Square.
Mille Fleurs was sold to the Government to serve as headquarters.
An extremist group held the prime minister and parliament hostage.
A series of bombings caused injuries to civilian bystanders.
A water taxi service linking the city with San Fernando restarted.
Trinidad and Tobago hosted the Fifth Summit of the Americas.
The performance centre was completed and hosted Queen Elizabeth II.
Wrightson Road natural gas-fired generation plant closed down permanently.
